chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salama ibn al-Khattab from Ali ibn Saif ibn 'Amirah from his father from Qutaybah al-A'sha from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the virtue/preference of the first time (of prayer) over the last time is like the virtue of the Hereafter over the world.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of performing prayers at their earliest time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration to underscore the jurisprudential principle of *ibtida'* (initiation) in prayer, highlighting that the spiritual reward for early performance is exponentially greater than mere fulfillment of the obligation. The analogy to the Hereafter versus the world reflects the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and the qualitative difference between performing acts promptly versus delaying them until the last moment. This hadith is frequently referenced in *usul al-fiqh* discussions regarding the distinction between the 'time of necessity' (*waqt al-hajah*) and the 'time of preference' (*waqt al-fadl*).
